title: Ephemeral KV shrinker race causing memory scarcity and GPU OOMs across private and dedicated clusters
creator: Marco Gutierrez
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (one Dedicated, two Private installs) reported sudden GPU OOMs during steady-state inference runs following rolling node drains and an automated compaction pass. Errors manifested as OOMs+session evictions with complementary metrics showing a rapid rise in small free-slab fragments and eviction-failure spikes. Host-operator noticed the first spike after a patch deployment that touched the KV compactor behavior. This ticket tracks the investigation, patch, and staged rollout.

Why this is unique: unlike previous large-allocation leaks, this failure mode is driven by a timing/race between the ephemeral KV shrinker (compactor) fast-path and the allocator coalesce path during node draining. The compactor was shrinking fragment lists while the allocator was concurrently merging arenas — in a narrow window this left many tiny free slots that the allocator refused to coalesce, causing headroom to evaporate for large tensor allocations and resulting in GPU OOMs. Private clusters showed the most severe failure because an older NVIDIA driver plus delayed GC made the window larger.

Affected surfaces: hosted (limited), dedicated (customers using medium-to-large reserved pools), private (on-prem customer X, managed customer Y). Severity: customer-facing P0 for Dedicated/Private customers.

How surfaced: customer alerting -> support escalation -> cluster logs -> heap/kv metric correlation. Key signals:
steps_taken:
- 2025-02-18 09:12 UTC: Support escalated from on-prem customer Y after two OOM incidents during a routine canary rollout.
- 2025-02-18 12:30 UTC: On-call reproduced high evict-fail-rate on a dev harness using node drains + compaction schedule.
- 2025-02-19 03:00 UTC: Instrumented compactor to emit shrinker-start/shrinker-end traces and added allocator coalesce tracepoints.
- 2025-02-19 09:45 UTC: Reproduced locally with stress harness: sequence of drain+compaction with synthetic small-key churn produced the same fragmentation pattern and OOM within ~45 minutes.
- 2025-02-20 15:20 UTC: Root-cause narrowed to ordering of compactor lock vs allocator arena lock under bursty eviction.
- 2025-02-21 01:10 UTC: Prototype patch created to ensure compactor runs under arena-coalescing-friendly critical section; added short backoff for compactor when allocator reports high coalesce backlog.
- 2025-02-22 07:30 UTC: Canary rollout to a Dedicated non-customer pool (5% nodes) with enhanced metrics. No OOMs after 40 hours soak.
- 2025-02-24 22:00 UTC: Emergency private customer build (cherry-pick) delivered to customer X for on-prem validation.
- 2025-02-25 11:00 UTC: Monitoring dashboards updated and alerts tuned (kv-frag-ratio, evict-fail-rate, allocator-headroom).
root_cause: A race between the KV compactor 'ephemeral shrinker' fast-path and the allocator's arena coalesce routine. The compactor would aggressively free many small fragments without holding the arena coalesce hold that guarantees subsequent merges. Under drain-heavy traffic the allocator attempted large tensor allocations which could not be satisfied because free memory was split into many sub-slab fragments. On some older GPU driver + OS combinations this pattern delayed physical memory reclamation and amplified the headroom loss leading to OOMs. The compactor fast-path prioritization, combined with lack of a short retry/backoff when evict/failure rates are high, exposed the allocator to pathological fragmentation.
mitigation:
Short-term: 1) Preventive circuit - disable the aggressive compactor fast-path on affected clusters (feature-flag rollback) and enable throttled compaction; 2) Emergency allocation backoff: allocator now applies a temporary bulk-evict request to the KV layer when allocation fails to create headroom; 3) For on-prem customer Y we shipped a cherry-pick that keeps compactor locked to arena coalesce entry.

Medium-term: 1) Patch compactor to acquire a cooperative coalesce token before bulk freeing and to yield when allocator coalesce backlog metric exceeds threshold; 2) Add allocator heuristics to actively coalesce tiny free-slab chains during low-load windows; 3) Driver/OS check at startup to detect delayed reclamation edge cases and throttle compaction accordingly.
resolution_notes:
Patch summary: runtime PR implements a cooperative coalesce token protocol between KV compactor and allocator and a saturating_eviction fallback when allocator headroom drops below 6% of pool. PRs: runtime#4367 mainline patch, runtime#4379 cherry-pick for 1.20.3-hotfix.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): 5% Dedicated nodes (completed 2025-02-22 soak 40h).
- Phase 2 (targeted fixes): deliver cherry-pick to affected Private customers (2025-02-24 deployed to customer X in lab).
- Phase 3 (gradual): 25% Dedicated + selected Hosted pods with tenant isolation enabled, monitor 7 days.
- Phase 4 (full): all Dedicated and Hosted nodes, regular Private packages released for on-prem customers.

Instrumentation added: kv-frag-ratio, compactor-latency, compactor-yields, allocator-coalesce-backlog, evict-fail-rate, per-tenant allocator-headroom. Alerts:
- kv-frag-ratio > 0.28 for 10m and evict-fail-rate > 1% -> PagerDuty
- allocator-headroom < 6% -> automated throttling of compactor fast-path
acceptance_criteria: No reproducible OOM in the dev stress harness with drain+compaction for 24h at production-like QPS
Canary Dedicated pool shows zero OOMs after 72h and metrics stable
Cherry-picked hotfix validated by on-prem customer X in their acceptance testbed
New metrics visible in Console with runbooks and alerts created

Merge to main and cut 1.20.3-hotfix branch with cherrypicks
